raw_response:
My land is about 7 mu of flat ground, same plot my husband and I have worked for thirty years. My son went to Shijiazhuang to work in a factory, so it's mostly me now. I don't read well, so I go by what I've done before and what the neighbors are doing.

Here in Quzhou this is what everyone does: wheat in winter, then maize after we harvest the wheat. Two crops on the same land every year. I have done this my whole life. My mother did it. There's no reason to change.

**Wheat (planted this October, harvested next June):**
I'll buy Jimai 22 seeds from the village shop like I did last year — they told me it resists rust disease. I put down compound fertilizer before plowing, then spread urea when the wheat turns green in spring and again at jointing. I pump water from the well four times: before winter sets in, again after the New Year when it greens up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. My yield last year was about 430 jin per mu, I'm hoping for the same. I'll spray herbicide once in winter and fungicide once in spring — that's what the village spraying team does.

**Maize (planted June after wheat, harvested September):**
Right after we cut the wheat I seed the maize directly into the stubble with the hand planter — no deep plowing in summer, too hot and the moisture escapes. I use Zhengdan 958, that hybrid everyone here uses. I spread all the fertilizer at once when planting because I can't always get back out for topdressing alone. I'll pump water twice if it doesn't rain enough — once when the seedlings are young and once at tasseling. I spray once or twice for corn borer and leaf blight.

I use a lot of fertilizer — my neighbor says I should use less but I'm afraid of a thin harvest. Better to use more than be sorry.
